newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - August 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - August 5.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on August 5. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Secretary-General of the ruling Golkar party Ary Mardjono hoped there will be no problems with the selection of the chairman of the national parliament after he returned from studying a case in Irian Jaya where Golkar members of the provincial legislature boycotted the swearing of the body's chairman in protest of the choice of candidate.

Satellite images have shown that the seasonal haze clouding Sumatra island, forcing the cancellation of some flights at a few airports, is the result of burning off after land has been cleared for plantations.
President Suharto urged government bureaucrats to be more sensitive toward people and not to treat them merely as objects who should obey their commands.
Senior ministers say the declining rupiah is a blessing in disguise for Indonesia's weakening non-oil exports as it would help drive up the demand for natural resource-based products.

Research and Technology Minister Habibie doubts the validity of the data and critera for a survey by Transparency International which found Indonesia the most corrupt nation in the nine-member Association of South East Asian Nations.

A traditional rivalry between two neighbours in east Jakarta broke out into a street riot on Sunday night with one car being burnt and number of people injured after stones were thrown before police controlled the situation.
